name: Archaeological Landscape of the First Coffee Plantations in the South-East of Cuba
description: In the steep foothills of the Sierra Maestra in southeastern Cuba, the ruins of more than 170 nineteenth-century coffee farms lie scattered through the forest. Settlers, many of them French planters who fled Haiti, cleared mountainsides to grow coffee, and they left behind stone-built drying floors, mills and owners' houses. Walking among them shows how enslaved labor and ingenuity made farming possible on difficult slopes.
